document.title: U.S. Requests Dubai Close Ariana (Afghan) Airlines: MBR Demurs, Saying it Would be Ineffective, But Leaves Door Ajar (State Department Cable 03508)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Newly Published Documents Cast Doubt on Claims Taliban Will Give Up al Qaeda | National Security Archive
document.note: [Secret] On May 29, Ambassador Theodore Kattouf asked Crown Prince Muhammad bin Rashid al Maktoum (MBR) to halt Ariana flights from Dubai, saying UBL was using Ariana to move men and material from Afghanistan via Dubai. MBR said he would consult advisors but that, with one weekly passenger flight, the move would likely be ineffective.

events.description: Secretary Cohen's letter on UBL and the executive order on the Taliban, requesting UAE deny landing rights to Ariana.
Chargé Jones delivered Cohen's letter and demarche to the UAE; response noncommittal.
actors: Government of the United Arab Emirates

events.description: Cable 05051 sent from Abu Dhabi to Washington.
President issued executive order imposing financial and commercial sanctions on the Taliban.
Bombings of two US embassies in East Africa (anniversary referenced).
Secretary Cohen's letter on bin Ladin and the Taliban executive order was sent to the UAE for delivery.
The chargé delivered Cohen's letter and asked the UAE to deny landing rights to Ariana Airlines and shut down its Dubai operations. The UAE response was noncommittal.
actors: Government of the United Arab Emirates

events.description: Embassy Abu Dhabi sent cable 005051 to Washington reporting the UAE's noncommittal response on Ariana.
The US cited the bombings of its two embassies in East Africa, whose anniversary was approaching, as context for the request.
The President issued an executive order imposing financial and commercial sanctions on the Taliban.

key_claims: The US believed UBL used Ariana Airlines to support terrorist activities and asked the UAE to close its Dubai operations.
The US judged the Taliban were continuing to support and protect UBL, prompting executive-order sanctions.
US officials warned UBL and followers were planning attacks on US personnel around the anniversary of the East Africa embassy bombings.
US believed UBL remained in Afghanistan despite press reports of leaving Qandahar, with unconfirmed rumors of ill health.
The UAE response was noncommittal, per the cable's summary.
